images.title: One strip of the chikki
images.purpose: Show that one strip is 1/3 of the chikki because 3 equal strips fill the whole, not 1/8 because it has 8 squares.
images.composition: The chikki grid on the left and one strip pulled out to its right, with wide space between, and one short line centred below.
images.exact_structure: Left: one chikki drawn as a grid of 24 equal small squares, 6 across and 4 down, cut by 2 thick upright lines into 3 equal strips of 2 across and 4 down; the strips are numbered 1, 2, 3 and outlined teal #0072B2. Right: one copy of a strip, 2 across and 4 down, 8 small squares, filled amber #E69F00, standing apart. Exactly 1 grid, 3 strips, 1 pulled out strip.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
strips of unequal width, or the pulled out strip drawn a different size from the strips in the grid
images.takeaway: Count the copies that fill the whole, not the squares: one strip is 1/3.
images.description: A 6 by 4 chikki grid cut into 3 equal numbered strips, with one strip of 8 squares pulled out and labelled 1/3; 3 × 8 = 24 squares checks it.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to point at the numbers 1, 2, 3 and say how many strips make the whole chikki.

image_decisions.why: Numbered strips filling the grid beside one pulled out strip show how to name a fractional unit by copies.
